title: OpenRAG: An open-source stack for RAG — Phil Nash

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk is primarily about OpenRAG, a RAG stack combining document processing, search indexing, and orchestration for retrieval-augmented generation. OpenRAG targets enterprise search and knowledge-base applications while also serving as an open-source developer platform for building RAG systems. The talk covers deployment configuration of a RAG stack and discusses evaluating outcomes with your data. The content assumes familiarity with RAG concepts, embeddings, and search but remains accessible to practitioners. This is a conference talk with live demonstrations of the OpenRAG system. summary: Phil Nash presents OpenRAG, an opinionated yet flexible open-source RAG stack from IBM that combines three existing open-source projects: Docling for document processing, OpenSearch for search indexing, and LangFlow for visual orchestration and agents. He begins by challenging the narrative that RAG is dead or trivially solved, emphasizing that RAG remains genuinely difficult due to PDF parsing challenges, evolving embedding models, complex chunking strategies, and constantly emerging search refinement techniques. OpenRAG addresses these challenges by providing a strong baseline that users can customize and evaluate. On the ingestion side, Docling processes HTML, markdown, Word documents, slides, spreadsheets, audio, video, and PDFs through specialized pipelines including a standard PDF pipeline with small focused models for layout analysis, table extraction, and OCR, plus a newer VLM pipeline using IBM's granite docling 258-million parameter vision model. Docling produces an intermediate XML-like representation called doc tags convertible to markdown, HTML, and JSON, with a chunker that respects document hierarchy. OpenRAG supports multiple embedding providers including OpenAI, watsonx AI, and Ollama for local execution, and can run entirely offline in air-gapped environments. OpenSearch provides hybrid vector and keyword search with sophisticated filtering and aggregation, supporting multiple embedding models simultaneously for migration scenarios, and defaults to the JVector KNN plugin for disk-based live indexing. LangFlow ties everything together as a drag-and-drop visual editor. OpenRAG uses agentic retrieval where the model decides which searches to perform rather than following a fixed top-K retrieval pipeline. The demonstration covers the chat interface, knowledge management with filters, cloud connectors, configurable ingestion, and model settings. Phil then shows deeper customization by editing the LangFlow flow directly, adding guardrails to the chat input, and revealing that OpenRAG exposes an MCP server and API for integration with other agents. He concludes that whether RAG is solved remains up to the user's data and needs, but OpenRAG provides a powerful, extensible open-source baseline currently at version 0.4.0, with the frontend built in Next.js and the rest in Python, welcoming community feedback and contributions to OpenRAG and its component projects.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: RAG is hard: Motivation for OpenRAG
sections.summary: Phil challenges the narrative that RAG is dead or trivially solved, citing PDF complexity, evolving embeddings, chunking strategy challenges, and emerging search refinement techniques as evidence that RAG remains genuinely difficult and project-specific.

sections.title: Introducing the OpenRAG stack
sections.summary: IBM built OpenRAG combining Docling for document processing, OpenSearch for search indexing, and LangFlow for visual orchestration, providing a powerful, easy-to-use, and extensible RAG baseline.

sections.title: Document processing with Docling
sections.summary: Docling handles HTML, markdown, Word, slides, spreadsheets, audio, video, and PDFs through specialized pipelines. The standard PDF pipeline uses small focused models for layout analysis, table extraction, and OCR. A newer VLM pipeline uses the granite docling 258-million parameter vision model. Output is an intermediate doc tags format convertible to markdown, HTML, and JSON, with a hierarchy-aware chunker.

sections.title: Embeddings and OpenSearch indexing
sections.summary: OpenRAG supports multiple embedding providers including OpenAI, watsonx AI, and Ollama for local execution, and can run fully offline. OpenSearch provides hybrid vector and keyword search with sophisticated filtering, supports multiple embedding models, and uses the JVector KNN plugin by default for disk-based live indexing that doesn't require the full index in memory.

sections.title: LangFlow orchestration and agentic retrieval
sections.summary: LangFlow is a drag-and-drop visual editor integrating Docling, OpenSearch, and embedding models. On the generation side, OpenRAG uses agentic retrieval where the model decides which searches to perform rather than following a fixed top-K pipeline, supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and watsonx AI models.

sections.title: Live demo: Chat and agentic search
sections.summary: Phil demonstrates the OpenRAG chat interface, showing tool calling in action when answering 'What is OpenRAG', agent-driven documentation search, and follow-up suggestion nudges powered by LangFlow.

sections.title: Knowledge section and cloud connectors
sections.summary: The knowledge section supports file and folder uploads, document and chunk inspection, sync functionality, and knowledge filter creation leveraging OpenSearch filtering. Settings include cloud connectors for Google Drive, SharePoint, and OneDrive via Google OAuth, configurable model providers, and agent system prompt customization.

sections.title: Ingestion and model configuration settings
sections.summary: Settings walkthrough shows local Granite 4 3B model via Ollama, Qwen 3 embedding 0.6B, configurable chunk size and overlap, and Docling options for table structure capture, OCR, and picture description extraction, plus API key management for external API access.

sections.title: Deep customization in LangFlow and MCP server
sections.summary: Phil demonstrates editing the LangFlow flow directly to add guardrails to chat input with a parser for pass-through and error handling. He shows the agent's tools including an MCP server URL ingestor, a calculator for arithmetic, and OpenSearch multi-model embedding. He reveals OpenRAG also exposes an MCP server and API for integration with other agents and applications.

sections.title: Conclusion: Is RAG solved?
sections.summary: Phil concludes that whether RAG is solved remains up to the user's data and needs, but OpenRAG provides an opinionated, agentic, open-source baseline at version 0.4.0. The frontend is Next.js with the rest in Python. He invites community feedback, GitHub stars, and contributions to OpenRAG and its component projects Docling, OpenSearch, and LangFlow.

limitations: Vector search over multiple embedding models slows down search in practice
Adding more models to the Docling pipeline such as OCR and picture descriptions makes ingestion slower
Cloud connectors require user model authentication setup with OAuth client and secret
Guardrail failures require manual routing of error messages to chat output
